sentences.text: Drusilasaura was an extinct giant sauropod dinosaur, a type of long-necked herbivore, possessing a massive scapula measuring 143 centimeters in length.
This shoulder blade was thirty percent longer than that of the related species Mendozasaurus.
Its specific name, deseadensis, refers to the nearby Río Deseado river.
If confirmed as a member of Lognkosauria, this animal would represent the oldest known member of that distinct group.
The genus name honors Drusila Ortiz de Zárate, the young woman who owned the ranch where the fossils were unearthed.
Paleontologist Marcelo Tejedor found the remains while searching for fossil mammals in the Upper Member of the Bajo Barreal Formation.
César Navarrete, Gabriel Casal, and Rubén Martínez formally named the genus in 2011.
Taxonomically, Drusilasaura belongs to the class Saurischia.
Researchers assigned it to the family Titanosauridae and considered it a possible member of the clade Lognkosauria.
This dinosaur lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
Its habitat was Santa Cruz Province in southern Patagonia, Argentina.
